[2026-05-31 22:48]

## Schema Audit Report — Rehearsal/Concert/Season/RSVP Domain

Source: `~/projects/entu-research/docs/schema/v4E/schema.ts` (v4E.0.1) + `~/workspace/src/` grep sweep.

---

## Part A — Current v4E Schema Shape

### `season` (Section 1.4)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `public`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parent:** `organization` (required, 1:0..N)
- **Properties:**
  - `name: string` (required, public) — e.g. "2025/2026 season"
  - `start_date: date` (required, public)
  - `end_date: date` (required, public)
  - `description: text` (public)
- **Creators:** `parent_right: _owner`
- **roleMapping:** `_editor → conductor`
- **Note:** "Conductor of season X = `_editor: <person>` on season X."

**Diff vs memory (`project_polyphony_seasons_events`):** Memory says `start_date` + `end_date` — matches exactly. No divergence.

---

### `event_series` (Section 1.4)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `public`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parents (multi-parent):**
  - `organization` (required, 1:0..N) — always present
  - `season` (optional, 0..N:0..N)
  - `section` (optional, 0..N:0..N)
- **Properties:**
  - `name: string` (required) — e.g. "Tuesday Rehearsals 2025/2026"
  - `event_type: string` (required) — enum: `rehearsal | concert | festival | retreat | workshop | meeting | social | other`
  - `interval_days: number` (required) — 7=weekly, 14=biweekly, 30≈monthly
  - `start_time: string` (required) — "HH:MM"
  - `duration_minutes: number` (required)
  - `start_date: date` (required) — first occurrence anchor
  - `end_date: date` (required) — last occurrence
  - `default_location: string`
  - `default_description: text`
- **Creators:** `parent_right: _editor`
- **roleMapping:** `_editor → conductor of series`
- **Note:** instance default `private`; admin flips to `public` for concert series.

**Diff vs memory:** Memory (`project_polyphony_seasons_events`) has `event_series` with `interval_days` + `start_time` + `duration` — schema uses `duration_minutes` (not `duration`). Memory is imprecise on the field name. Also: schema has `event_series` as a PARENT of `event` (optional `0..1`) — that parent relationship is the v4E design, not just a reference property.

---

### `event` (Section 1.4)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `public`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parents (multi-parent):**
  - `organization` (required, 1:0..N) — always
  - `season` (optional, 0..N:0..N)
  - `section` (optional, 0..N:0..N)
  - `event_series` (optional, 0..1:0..N) — "instance of"
- **Properties:**
  - `name: string` (inherited from series.name if not set)
  - `event_type: string` (inherited from series.event_type if not set) — same enum as series
  - `start_datetime: datetime` (required)
  - `duration_minutes: number` (inherited from series if not set)
  - `location: string` (inherited from series.default_location if not set)
  - `description: text` (inherited from series.default_description if not set)
  - `capacity: number` — optional venue/attendance cap
- **Creators:** `parent_right: _editor`
- **roleMapping:** `_editor → conductor (event scope) / guest conductor of event`
- **Notes:**
  - No `status` field — cancellation = delete.
  - BFF series-regeneration must not blindly recreate deleted dates.
  - Instance default `private`; series-level `_sharing` cascades to children via BFF.

**Key design point — rehearsal vs concert distinction:** There is NO separate `rehearsal` or `concert` entity type. The `event_type` string property (on both `event` and `event_series`) carries this: `rehearsal | concert | festival | retreat | workshop | meeting | social | other`.

**Diff vs memory:** Memory mentions `event` is multi-parent (org + season(s) + section(s) + series) — correct. Memory also mentions `capacity` as a PR #41 addition — it IS present in schema.ts. Inheritance of unset properties from parent series is described as "BFF-mediated" — that's not automated Entu magic, it's a BFF read-time concern. Memory matches.

---

### `rsvp` (Section 1.5)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `private`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parent:** `person` (required, 1:0..N)
- **Properties:**
  - `event: event` (ref, required)
  - `member: member` (ref, required) — per-org context
  - `status: string` (required) — `going | not_going | maybe`
  - `notes: text`
- **Creators:** `self`
- **Notes:**
  - "Private — person sees own; admins/conductors aggregate via BFF report."
  - `organization.rsvp_lockout_hours`: 0 = soft warning; positive = hard block (on `organization` entity, not `rsvp`).

**Diff vs memory (`project_polyphony_participation`):** Memory says `rsvp` = child of person, member-created — **matches**. Status values `going | not_going | maybe` not mentioned in memory but now confirmed in schema. Memory is incomplete here; schema is the source.

---

### `attendance` (Section 1.5)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `private`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parent:** `event` (required, 1:0..N)
- **Properties:**
  - `member: member` (ref, required)
  - `status: string` (required) — `present | absent | late`
  - `notes: text` — e.g. "left after intermission"
- **Creators:** `parent_right: _editor` (conductor-created)
- **Note:** "Excused absence derivable from rsvp + attendance combination — no separate flag."

**Diff vs memory:** Memory says `attendance` = child of event, conductor-created — **matches**. Status values `present | absent | late` now confirmed. No divergence.

---

### `repertoire_item` (Section 1.4)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `public`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parent:** `season` (required, 1:0..N)
- **Properties:**
  - `name: string` — formula: `work.*.name CONCAT`
  - `work: work` (ref, required)
  - `edition: edition` (ref, optional) — preferred/pinned edition for this season
  - `status: string` — `learning | active | retired | dropped`; default `active`
- **Creators:** `parent_right: _editor`

**Diff vs memory (`project_polyphony_programs`):** Memory mentions `repertoire_item` as child of season — **matches**. Status field (`learning | active | retired | dropped`) is confirmed present. Memory is aligned.

---

### `program_item` (Section 1.4)

- **Present:** yes
- **Sharing:** `public`; `inheritsRights: true`
- **Parent:** `event` (required, 1:0..N)
- **Properties:**
  - `name: string` — formula: `edition.*.work CONCAT` (work name via edition's `work` formula)
  - `edition: edition` (ref, required)
  - `ordinal: number` (required) — position in concert programme
  - `notes: text` — soloists, dedications
- **Creators:** `parent_right: _editor`
- **Notes:** `_sharing` matches parent event's (BFF cascade).

**Diff vs memory:** Memory mentions `name` as single-hop formula via `edition.work` — confirmed. Memory matches.

---

### Referenced entity bits (just the relevant fields)

| Entity | Relevant to domain |
|---|---|
| `person` | parent of `rsvp`; `_sharing: public` |
| `member` | referenced by `rsvp.member` + `attendance.member`; `_sharing: private`; parent: org (required) + section (optional) |
| `section` | optional parent of `event_series` and `event` (section-scoped events) |
| `organization` | parent of `season`, `event_series`, `event`; carries `rsvp_lockout_hours: number` |

---

## Part B — What mvox Already Has Wired

**Short answer: near-zero, as expected.** The only hits touching this domain are:

### Routes

- `src/routes/library/` — has `/library` route only. No `/season`, `/event`, `/rehearsal`, `/concert`, `/rsvp`, `/attendance` routes exist.

### Types / fixtures

- `src/lib/types/library.ts:8` — `Choir` interface has `rehearsal_size: number`. This is a mock-data field on the local `Choir` type, not a v4E entity property.
- `src/lib/fixtures/library-mock.ts:10` — `rehearsal_size: 48` on the mock choir constant.
- `src/lib/fixtures/library-mock.ts:33,384` — string literals "December concert" in lending notes/history text — plain prose, not entity references.

### Components / routes using mock data

- `src/routes/library/+page.svelte:85` — renders `m.library_rehearsal_in({ time: '16:00', countdown: '1h 28m' })` — **hardcoded mock only**, no live event/season data fetching.

[2026-05-31 23:12] VERDICT: **GREEN** — data model + rights flow are sound for the first slice. Two YELLOWs (design-clarifications, not blockers) + one must-state invariant. Verified against `schema.ts` (not from memory) — season L626, event_series L663, event L726, organization L151.

**The model matches canonical v4E almost exactly.** season/event_series/event already exist in `schema.ts` with the parents, props, creators, and sharing you proposed. Nothing here needs a Schema-Change trailer — it's schema-alignment (building to an already-landed shape), per the carve-out.

PER-POINT:

**Q1 — owner/editor split + membership-pairing: GREEN.** season `creators: parent_right _owner` (L658), series + event `_editor` (L719, L784) — matches schema verbatim. Single admin-conductor persona holding `_owner` on org cascades nothing by itself BUT — see the must-state below — `inheritsRights:true` on season means `_owner`-on-org would flow IF org weren't the island. The membership-pairing invariant (every `_owner`/`_editor`/`_viewer` grant requires an active `member`) is NOT tripped in this slice: you're not granting rights to other people; the admin already has their grants from being the org admin (which presupposes their own `member`). The N generated events are created BY that admin under their existing `_editor` — no NEW grants minted. Clean.

**Q2 — explicit `_sharing` at create: GREEN, but note the type-vs-instance split.** Your plan (season=public, series=private, event=private) is correct AND matches the schema's instance-default guidance: season type+instance both `public` (L629); series type `public` / **instance default `private`** (L722 note); event type `public` / **instance default `private`** (L788 note). So season=public, series=private, event=private is exactly right. Per `project_entu_sharing_non_inherit`, BFF sets it explicitly on every POST — confirmed needed, no inheritance.

**Q3 — eager materialization OFF elevated-ops: CONFIRMED GREEN.** ~35 serial POSTs as the authenticated conductor under their own `_editor` is textbook user-rights-default creation. It does NOT belong on the elevated-ops list — no secret, no privilege beyond the user's own rights, the user could do each POST by hand in any Entu frontend. This is the open-platform stance working as intended. (Perf note, not a rights note: 35 serial POSTs is fine; if it ever feels slow, that's a UX/batching question, never a reason to elevate.)

**Q4 — read-time BFF inheritance, not formula: AGREED, GREEN.** The schema is explicit and on your side — every inherited event prop says "inherited from series.X if not set" as a NOTE (L764-777), and the blurb says "read-time, BFF-mediated" (L729). NONE are declared as `formula`. So zero multi-hop-formula risk: the inheritance is BFF application logic reading both entities and merging, not Entu evaluating a traversal. **Where a formula trap WOULD sneak in (watch for it in the spec):** if anyone "optimizes" event.name/location/etc. into an Entu `formula: 'event_series.*.default_location'`-style prop to avoid the BFF merge. That's the trap — (a) `event_series` is a `0..1` parent so it's a single hop, BUT (b) the inherited values are raw strings (location, description, name) and **the formula evaluator bypasses rights** — projecting series.default_description onto a public-ish event read would leak across the series-private boundary. Keep inheritance in the BFF. If the spec ever says "formula" for any of these six inherited props → RED.

**MUST-STATE INVARIANT (the one thing your summary didn't mention, and it's load-bearing):** the rights flow only works because **`organization` is `inheritsRights: false` (L155) — the lone island in the whole schema** — while **season, event_series, event are all `inheritsRights: true` (L630, L668, L731).** Consequence the spec must encode: granting the conductor `_editor` on the SEASON cascades down to its event_series and events automatically (that's how the conductor can edit/cancel the generated events without a per-event grant). And the org boundary stops any of this from leaking UP to the umbrella. So the demo persona needs exactly two explicit grants: `_owner` on org (admin) + `_editor` on season (conductor) — events inherit editor from season. Don't grant `_editor` per-event; that's redundant and would muddy the membership-pairing audit. State this cascade in the spec so Tallis tests it and nobody "helpfully" adds per-event grants.

**YELLOW-1 (spec-clarity): cancellation = DELETE, and regeneration must respect deletions.** Schema event note L787: *"No `status` field — cancellation = delete. BFF series-regeneration must not blindly recreate deleted dates."* Your slice says "cancel/edit a single instance" — cancel is a hard `DELETE /entity/{eventId}`, there is no soft-cancel flag. The trap: if the conductor later edits the SERIES (e.g., extends end_date) and the BFF re-materializes, a naive regen recreates the cancelled date. The spec needs a regeneration-idempotency rule (e.g., regen only fills gaps forward of existing+the series anchor set, or tracks a cancelled-dates ledger). Not a blocker for slice-1 if "edit series → regenerate" is out of scope, but call the boundary explicitly so it's a known deferred, not a silent gap. Flag for test-gaps.md either way.

**YELLOW-2 (spec-clarity): `start_time` is a STRING "HH:MM" but event `start_datetime` is a real `datetime`.** Schema: series.start_time `type: string` "19:00" (L712); event.start_datetime `type: datetime` (L766). The eager-materialization BFF must compose `start_date + interval_days*n` (date math) with `start_time` (string parse) into a proper `datetime` per occurrence — and get the timezone right (Estonia/Latvia DST shifts across a Sep–May season: a "19:00" rehearsal is 19:00 EET in winter, 19:00 EEST in summer — the wall-clock string is stable, the UTC offset is not). The spec should pin whether start_datetime is stored as local-wall-clock or UTC, because a Sep-to-May weekly series crosses the DST boundary twice. Cheap to get right at design time, painful to retrofit. Not a rights issue — a correctness one — so YELLOW.

Nothing else rises to RED. The skeleton is schema-faithful and the rights story is coherent. Ready for you to write the spec; I'll review it against this verdict when it lands.
summary: GREEN with 2 YELLOW — rehearsal-schedule data model sound

[2026-05-31 23:12] AC draft for the rehearsal-schedule first slice. Structured by capability, with issue disposition at the end.

---

## AC: Rehearsal Schedule — First Buildable Slice

---

### Capability 1 — Create Season
*Extends existing #19 ADMIN-1. The AC below replaces the stub there.*

**Rights:** `_owner` on org only.

1. Admin sees a "Create season" form with fields: name (required), start_date (required), end_date (required), description (optional).
2. `end_date >= start_date` — BFF validates; returns 400 with field-level error message on violation; UI shows inline error beneath end_date field without clearing other fields.
3. `name` may not be blank or whitespace-only — BFF validates; returns 400.
4. On success, BFF creates `season` entity with `_parent = org`; responds 201 with the new entity's `_id`.
5. Newly created season appears at the top of the org's season list (chronological by start_date).
6. Non-`_owner` (e.g. conductor, singer) attempting POST → BFF returns 403; UI shows permission error.
7. **Empty state:** org has no seasons → admin sees "No seasons yet — create your first season" CTA; conductor/singer sees "Season not yet set up."

**Vitest:**
- Season created with valid fields → 201 + entity `_id` returned
- `end_date < start_date` → 400 with `end_date` error key
- `end_date = start_date` → 201 (same-day season is valid)
- Blank name → 400 with `name` error key
- Non-owner auth token → 403

---

### Capability 2 — Create Rehearsal Series
*Extends existing #20 ADMIN-2 (series half). The AC below should be merged into or appended to that issue.*

**Rights:** `_editor` on org (conductor) or `_owner` on org (admin).

1. Conductor or admin sees a "Create rehearsal series" form, available from within a season context (season must exist first — Capability 1 gates this).
2. Required fields: name, interval_days (positive integer ≥ 1), start_time (HH:MM, 24h), duration_minutes (positive integer ≥ 1), start_date, end_date.
3. Optional fields: default_location (string), default_description (string).
4. `event_type` is fixed to `rehearsal` — not a user-selectable field in this slice (the form pre-sets it, BFF enforces it).
5. `start_date` and `end_date` are scoped within the parent season's date range — BFF validates; returns 400 if series start_date < season start_date or series end_date > season end_date.
6. `end_date >= start_date` — BFF validates; returns 400 on violation.
7. On success, BFF creates `event_series` entity with `_parent` references: org + season. Responds 201 with the series `_id`.
8. Non-editor/non-owner attempting POST → BFF returns 403.

**Vitest:**
- Valid series payload → 201 + series `_id`
- `interval_days = 0` → 400
- `interval_days = -1` → 400
- Series `start_date` before season `start_date` → 400 with `start_date` error key
- Series `end_date` after season `end_date` → 400 with `end_date` error key
- Non-conductor auth token (singer) → 403
- `event_type` in payload overridden to anything other than `rehearsal` → BFF silently forces `rehearsal` (no 400; documented behavior)

---

### Capability 3 — Generate Event Instances (Eager)
*NEW — no existing issue. Recommend filing ADMIN-6.*

**Trigger:** Immediately on successful `event_series` creation (synchronous in the BFF response cycle for v1 — no background job).

**Rights:** same as series creator (conductor or admin).

1. BFF computes occurrence dates: starting from series `start_date`, stepping by `interval_days`, collecting every date `<= series end_date`.
2. For each occurrence date, BFF creates one `event` entity:
   - `_parent` references: org + season + the new `event_series`
   - `event_type = rehearsal`
   - `start_datetime` = occurrence date + series `start_time` (ISO 8601, UTC stored, local display in UI)
   - `duration_minutes` = series `duration_minutes`
   - `location` = series `default_location` (may be absent)
   - `description` = series `default_description` (may be absent)
   - `_sharing = private`
3. Event count is deterministic: `floor((end_date - start_date) / interval_days) + 1`.
4. BFF returns the series creation response (201) only after all events are created. If any event creation fails mid-batch, BFF returns 500 and reports how many events were created before failure (partial state — conductor must delete and retry; no rollback in v1).
5. Manually deleted events are NOT recreated on any subsequent operation (generation is one-shot at series creation; no regeneration in this slice).

**Vitest:**
- Series with `start_date=2026-09-01`, `end_date=2026-09-29`, `interval_days=7` → exactly 5 events created at dates 09-01, 09-08, 09-15, 09-22, 09-29
- Series with `start_date=2026-09-01`, `end_date=2026-09-01`, `interval_days=7` → exactly 1 event created
- Series with `start_date=2026-09-01`, `end_date=2026-09-08`, `interval_days=7` → exactly 2 events (boundary inclusive)
- Each generated event carries correct `start_datetime` combining occurrence date + series `start_time`
- Each generated event has `_parent` includes org, season, and series IDs
- Generated events have `event_type = rehearsal`
- Generated events have `_sharing = private`

---

### Capability 4 — View Generated Rehearsal List
*NEW — no existing issue. Recommend filing ADMIN-7.*

**Rights:** `_editor` or `_owner` on org (conductor or admin). Singer view is out of scope for this slice.

1. Conductor sees a rehearsal list page at `/[orgId]/rehearsals` (or `/[orgId]/seasons/[seasonId]/rehearsals` — Palestrina to decide route shape).
2. BFF queries `event` entities where: `_parent.reference` includes the org, `event_type = rehearsal`. Ordered by `start_datetime` ascending.
3. Each row shows: date (human-readable, user locale), time, duration_minutes, location (if set; otherwise "—"), series name (for grouping context).
4. Events are grouped visually by `event_series` parent (series name as section header). Events not belonging to any series (standalone rehearsals, if any) appear under "Ungrouped."
5. Past events (start_datetime < now) are visible but visually de-emphasised (muted style, not hidden).
6. **Empty state:** season has no rehearsals → "No rehearsals scheduled yet" with CTA to create a series.
7. List is server-side rendered (`+page.server.ts` load).
8. The list does NOT show RSVP counts, attendance, or programme in this slice.

**Vitest:**
- BFF returns events ordered by `start_datetime` ascending
- Events filtered to `event_type = rehearsal` only (concert-type events not returned)
- Empty result → 200 with empty array (not 404)

**Playwright (E2E — noted, can be deferred per Tallis's discretion):**
- Conductor logged in → navigates to rehearsal list → sees events grouped by series with correct dates

---

### Capability 5 — Cancel / Edit a Single Instance
*NEW — no existing issue. Recommend filing ADMIN-8.*

**Rights:** `_editor` or `_owner` on org.

#### 5a. Cancel (delete) a single event

1. Conductor selects a single rehearsal from the list → confirms cancel action.
2. BFF deletes the `event` entity (`DELETE /entity/{eventId}`).
3. Sibling events (same series) are unaffected — BFF fetches and confirms count before and after; only the targeted entity is removed.
4. The series `event_series` entity itself is NOT deleted.
5. On success, the deleted event disappears from the rehearsal list immediately (UI removes row optimistically or re-fetches).
6. Cancelling the LAST remaining event in a series → event deleted, series entity remains (orphaned series is valid state in v1).

**Vitest:**
- DELETE on event `_id` → 200; sibling events still exist
- Attempting DELETE with singer auth token → 403
- Attempting DELETE on an event that doesn't exist → 404

#### 5b. Edit a single instance (override inherited fields)

1. Conductor selects a single rehearsal → opens edit form pre-populated with current values.
2. Editable fields on a single instance: `start_datetime` (date+time), `duration_minutes`, `location`, `description`.
3. `event_type` and `_parent` references are NOT editable on a single instance.
4. BFF PATCHes the `event` entity properties directly (clear existing property value, POST new value per Entu POST-appends pattern).
5. Edited instance retains its overrides across list re-loads — it does NOT re-inherit series defaults.
6. Sibling events are unaffected by the edit.
7. Series-level fields (`interval_days`, `start_time`, `duration_minutes`) are NOT editable in this slice — only per-instance overrides.

**Vitest:**
- PATCH event with new `location` → GET event returns updated location; sibling events unchanged
- PATCH event with new `start_datetime` → event carries override; siblings at original times
- PATCH with singer auth → 403
- PATCH on non-existent event `_id` → 404

---

## Issue Disposition

| Capability | Action | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Create season | **Update #19** (replace stub AC with above) | Same story, richer AC |
| 2 — Create rehearsal series | **Update #20** (append series-specific AC above; mark concerts/concerts-series out of scope for this slice) | Same story, scope narrowed |
| 3 — Generate event instances | **File NEW issue ADMIN-6** | Zero coverage today; BFF logic is substantial |
| 4 — View rehearsal list | **File NEW issue ADMIN-7** | Zero coverage; this is the "primary screen" gap I flagged |
| 5 — Cancel/edit single instance | **File NEW issue ADMIN-8** | Zero coverage; two sub-capabilities (5a + 5b), could split if needed |

**My recommendation:** file ADMIN-6/7/8 as a bundle with `admin, conductor` labels and no milestone (same as ADMIN-1/2). Split 5a and 5b into separate issues only if you expect them to land in different TDD cycles — the AC is separable.

Holding on `gh issue` commands until you confirm disposition and give go-ahead.

[2026-05-31 23:41] VERDICT on spec `8a5887a`: **YELLOW** — faithful encoding of my GREEN verdict, Capability 6 is sound, BUT the §8 delete-rights probe is more load-bearing than the spec treats it, and the schema evidence already leans toward an answer that would reshape Cap 5a + Cap 6. Not RED (you correctly flagged it as a pre-GREEN probe), but elevating it from "open question" to "likely-blocking assumption" so it's resolved before the plan locks the rights story. Verified against case-study + README this turn (not from memory).

**THE BIG ONE — Q4 (delete rights): the schema evidence says `_editor` probably CANNOT delete. Your probe instinct was right; don't let the spec's prose ("assumes `_editor` suffices") harden into the plan.**

Two sources, and they disagree at exactly the layer that matters:
- **README role-table (`README.md:513-515`)** says Conductor (`_editor` on season) has **"full"** on season/event_series/event. Read alone, this backs the spec's assumption.
- **BUT the case-study tier definitions (`2026-05-polyphony-on-entu.md:29-31`) — which is the live-Entu-verified mechanics layer** — say:
  - `_owner`: full control **+ delete** + manage rights
  - `_editor`: read + **edit properties** (except rights props) — **no delete listed**
  - `_expander`: read + create children

So at Entu's actual permission-engine level, **DELETE is an `_owner`-only capability.** The README's "full" for conductor is role-design aspiration; the tier mechanics are what Entu actually enforces, and they put delete above `_editor`. When a documented role-table and the verified tier-mechanics disagree, the tier-mechanics win (they're what the API enforces) — this is exactly the kind of load-bearing identifier my new arch-decision says to verify against ground truth rather than assert.

**Consequence if the probe confirms `_editor`-can't-delete (likely):**

## Cap 7 AC gaps / questions

**1. Which entity receives the `_editor` grant — season or org? (wording ambiguity)**

The spec says "direct `_editor` grant on the season," and the cascade logic ("can now POST a series under the season via cascade") follows from that correctly. But AC item 5 says the BFF reads "directly-granted `_editor`s" to build the conductor list. The test case says "cascaded org-`_owner` admin is NOT listed as a conductor" — which implies the BFF distinguishes direct grants on the season from inherited grants from the org level.

The ambiguity: does Entu's rights API return enough metadata to distinguish *direct* vs *cascaded* grants on a given entity? If it doesn't (i.e., the read gives you a flat merged set), the "list conductors" AC is unimplementable without a separate data structure. This is exactly what probe #4 should answer — but if Pérotin's probe shows the API returns a flat set, the AC for item 5 breaks.

Suggest adding to probe #4: "confirm GET /entity/{seasonId} rights view separates direct vs inherited grantees."

**2. Unassign: what happens to events the conductor already created?**

AC item 6 says "the person loses season edit access (and the cascade to its series/events)." That's the rights side. But what about `event_series` or `event` entities the conductor created as `_owner` (creator is auto-granted `_owner` on the created entity in Entu)? Revoking their season `_editor` doesn't revoke the entity-level `_owner` they hold on their own events.

The AC is silent on this. Two options:
- (A) Acceptable gap: unassigning a conductor only removes their ability to *create new* series/events; they retain edit access to ones they already created. V1 acceptable state — document it explicitly.
- (B) BFF must cascade-delete or cascade-revoke entity-level grants on the conductor's created entities at unassign time. Expensive and risky.

I'd recommend (A) with an explicit note in the AC. **Your call.**

**3. Display name resolution for conductor list (single-hop rule)**

AC item 5 says "resolves person display names (single-hop)." ADMIN-5 has the same pattern (member.person → separate fetch). The gotcha from my scratchpad applies: `_editor` grants likely expose a person entity reference, but person display names require a separate BFF fetch per person (no formula chain). That's fine — just needs to be explicit in the AC the same way ADMIN-5 spells it out. The current text says "single-hop" but doesn't say what property to read or that it requires a separate API call per person.

Suggest: "BFF resolves person display names via a separate `GET /entity/{personId}` fetch per grantee (single-hop; not formula-traversable, per v4E rule)."

---

## My read overall

Cap 7 is clean on the key decisions: roles-as-rights (no `conductors` property), `_owner`-only assignment, membership-pairing invariant, and the cascade direction (season → series → events, not per-event grants). The three items above are refinements, not redesigns. If you want I can draft the expanded AC text for ADMIN-10 incorporating these, once you decide on gap #2.

Your three rights claims all CONFIRM, and the mechanics question you were least sure of has a verified-against-live-Entu answer that backs your design.

**Your three rights claims — all CONFIRMED:**

1. **Grant/revoke `_editor` = `_owner`-tier: CORRECT.** Case-study tier-mechanics (`2026-05-polyphony-on-entu.md:29`): `_owner` = "manage rights"; `_editor` = "edit properties (except rights properties)". Rights props (`_editor`/`_owner`/etc.) are explicitly outside `_editor`'s reach, so granting/revoking a conductor is owner-only. An `_editor` conductor → 403 on assign (AC7) is exactly right.

2. **User-rights-default, NOT elevated: CORRECT.** Same reasoning as Cap 3 — the owner manages rights with their OWN `_owner`, which they could do in any Entu frontend. No secret, no privilege beyond the user's own tier. Stays OFF the elevated-ops list. Clean.

3. **Membership-pairing enforced: CORRECT and load-bearing.** This is the `project_polyphony_roles_as_rights` + membership-rights invariant (`README.md:522-527`) working exactly as designed: "any explicit `_owner`/`_editor`/`_viewer` grant on an org-subtree entity MUST be paired with an active `member`." BFF refusing to grant `_editor` to a non-member (400 "must be an org member first", AC4) is the invariant's enforcement point. Textbook.

**YOUR HARD QUESTION — "can the BFF distinguish a DIRECT `_editor` on the season from the org-owner's cascaded/inherited rights?" — YES, cleanly, and it's verified-live:**

Case-study `2026-05-polyphony-on-entu.md:48` (verified against live Entu, entu/www#2): *"Inheritance is **materialized** (the inherited rights are physically written to the child's rights properties). When reading the child, the inherited entries appear marked with `inherited: true`."*

So when the BFF GETs the season entity, the rights properties carry BOTH the direct grants AND the cascaded org-`_owner`'s materialized entries — but **the cascaded ones are flagged `inherited: true`** and the direct conductor grants are not. "List conductors = direct `_editor`s minus cascaded org-owner" is wire-sound: **filter the season's `_editor` list to entries WITHOUT `inherited: true`.** Your AC5 ("directly-granted `_editor`s, excluding the cascaded org-`_owner` admin") is computable on the wire as written. This was the one place you flagged uncertainty — it's solid.

**TWO WIRE-NUANCES to fold into §8 probe #4 (not blockers — they make the probe confirm the right things):**

- **(a) The `inherited: true` flag is "undocumented but verified" per the case study.** It's the lynchpin of AC5's list computation, so the probe should explicitly CONFIRM it surfaces in the season GET response shape mvox actually receives (the case study verified it on a 5-level chain via entu/www#2; confirm it's present in OUR read path). If for some reason the flag isn't exposed in the API shape the BFF sees, AC5 needs a fallback (e.g., cross-reference the org's `_owner` list and subtract those person-ids from the season's `_editor` list — derivable, just more work). Add to probe #4: "confirm the season GET exposes `inherited: true` on cascaded rights entries so direct-vs-inherited is distinguishable."

- **(b) Tier-cascade on grant — granting `_editor: X` materializes `_editor + _expander + _viewer` for X** (case study L50). This is fine — they're lower tiers of the SAME direct grant to the same person, not extra people. But it means AC5's list must read the **`_editor` list specifically** (not `_viewer`, which will also contain X plus every member's viewer-sync). The spec already says "reads the season's directly-granted `_editor`s" — correct as written; just flag for the plan that the list query targets the `_editor` property precisely, since `_viewer` is noisier (every basic member gets a `_viewer` cascade per `README.md:490`). And on **unassign** (AC6 "deletes that `_editor` grant value"): deleting the `_editor` entry is the right primitive — Entu's tier mechanics drop the materialized `_expander`/`_viewer` with it (they were materialized FROM the `_editor` grant). The probe should confirm revoke cleanly removes the whole tier-cascade, not just the `_editor` line leaving orphan `_expander`/`_viewer`. Worth one assertion in probe #4.

**Propagation-timing footnote (plan-level, not spec-level):** post-grant rights propagation is ~1.5-3.5s PER inheritance level (case study L54, verified). So after an assign, the new conductor's cascade to series/events isn't instant — a write-then-immediately-read on a grandchild event may not yet reflect the grant. AC7's "can now POST a series under the season" test and the UI's optimistic conductor-list update should tolerate that lag (poll/re-fetch, or assert with a retry window). Not a spec change — a test-harness + UX note for the plan so nobody writes a flaky immediate-read assertion.

**Net: GREEN.** Cap 7 is architecturally sound, matches roles-as-rights, all three rights claims hold, and the direct-vs-inherited list computation is verified-wire-sound via the `inherited: true` flag. Fold nuances (a)+(b) into §8 probe #4 and carry the propagation-timing note into the plan's test design. Everything I previously GREEN'd is unchanged. **The whole spec is cleared for writing-plans.** Nice — Model A over a `conductors` property was the right PO call; it keeps zero schema change and makes the rights model the single source of truth for "who conducts."

## P0.2 — Conductor grant wire
**CONFIRMED.**

Grant: `POST /db/entity/{seasonId}` with body `[{ "type": "_editor", "reference": "<personId>" }]`
Response: `{ "_id": "<seasonId>", "properties": [{ "_id": "<propValueId>", "type": "_editor", "reference": "<personId>" }] }`

The response `properties` array contains ONLY the newly-added property — read `properties[0]._id` directly for the revoke value ID. No separate GET needed.

Revoke: `DELETE /db/property/{propValueId}` → HTTP 200. Post-revoke count = 0. Clean.

---

## P0.3 — `inherited: true` flag — CONFIRMED, with a critical nuance for Tallis

**Flag IS present.** The `listConductors` implementation CAN filter direct vs inherited using the flag.

**Critical nuance:** The `_editor` field on GET entity is a **flattened rights view** that mixes `_owner` AND `_editor` entries. A `property_type` field on each entry distinguishes them. Raw observed field (after direct `_editor` grant):

```json
[
  { "_id": "69bd...", "reference": "69bcfd8e9c031ab8e6ce807a", "property_type": "_owner", "string": "polyphony", "entity_type": "database", "inherited": true },
  { "_id": "6a1cd2...", "reference": "<conductorPersonId>", "property_type": "_editor", "string": "_probe_conductor_person", "entity_type": "person" },
  { "_id": "6a1cd2...", "reference": "69bcfd8e9c031ab8e6ce8079", "property_type": "_owner", "string": "Mihkel Putrinš", "entity_type": "person" }
]
```

**The correct `listConductors` filter is:**
```typescript
entity._editor
  .filter(e => e.property_type === '_editor')   // exclude _owner entries
  .filter(e => e.inherited !== true)             // exclude inherited cascades
```

The simple `!inherited` filter is NOT safe — the PO's direct `_owner` entry has `inherited: undefined` (not `false`), so it would pass the `!inherited` guard. `property_type === '_editor'` filtering is required.

The spec §8 #4 org-owner-subtraction fallback is **not needed** — the flag is present and `property_type` handles the rest.

**Action for Tallis (Task 10 RED):** The `listConductors` spec in the plan's Step 1 test already uses `inherited: false` on the direct conductor entry. That test needs updating: the correct shape is `inherited: undefined` (field absent) on direct entries, not `inherited: false`. And the test should also assert that `_owner` entries (even without `inherited`) are excluded via `property_type` filtering. See the raw field above.

---

## P0.4 — Revoke drops tier-cascade
**CONFIRMED.** Pre-revoke: `_expander` = 1, `_viewer` = 1 (cascade materialised). Post-revoke (after ~1s): both 0. No orphans. A single `DELETE /property/{propValueId}` is sufficient.

---

## P0.5 — Creator auto-owner?
**CONFIRMED.** Creator gets entity-level `_owner` automatically. The Cap6 residual-rights edge in spec §7 is real: a conductor who creates rehearsal events retains `_owner` on those events after their conductor grant is revoked (until those entities are separately reassigned or deleted). This is Entu's documented model, not a bug. Worth surfacing in the UI ("deleting a series removes all its events").

---

## P0.6 — Propagation timing
**CONFIRMED.** Lag = **193ms** (succeeded on first attempt). The spec's "~1.5–3.5s/level" was a conservative upper bound. For the test-harness retry window (Task 15): a 500ms initial delay with 2–3 retries at 500ms each is more than sufficient.

## Draft `seasons_*` Key Manifest

### Season form labels (Cap 1 — SeasonForm)

| Key | en value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `seasons_form_season_heading` | `New season` | Form heading |
| `seasons_field_name` | `Name` | Season name field label; reused on series form too |
| `seasons_field_start_date` | `Start date` | |

| `seasons_field_description` | `Description` | Optional field; also on series form |
| `seasons_form_season_submit` | `Create season` | Submit button |

### Series form labels (Cap 2 — SeriesForm)

| Key | en value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `seasons_form_series_heading` | `New rehearsal series` | Form heading |
| `seasons_field_interval_days` | `Repeat every (days)` | `interval_days` — integer input; "days" stays in the label to clarify the unit |
| `seasons_field_start_time` | `Start time` | `start_time`; HH:MM hint |
| `seasons_field_duration` | `Duration (minutes)` | `duration_minutes`; "minutes" in label to clarify unit |
| `seasons_field_location` | `Location` | Optional; shared with single-event edit form (Cap 5b) |
| `seasons_form_series_submit` | `Create series` | Submit button |

### Validation error messages (keyed by `code` from `validateSeason` / `validateSeries`)

These are inline field errors. The `code` values come directly from `validation.ts` as defined in Plan Task 2.

| Key | en value | `code` it covers | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seasons_error_blank` | `Required` | `blank` | All blank-name validations |
| `seasons_error_end_before_start` | `End date must be on or after start date` | `end_before_start` | Used on both season and series end-date fields |
| `seasons_error_interval_too_small` | `Must be at least 1 day` | `interval_too_small` | Series intervalDays |
| `seasons_error_outside_season` | `Must fall within the season's dates` | `outside_season` | Series start/end outside season range |

**Note on `seasons_error_outside_season`:** the plan's `validateSeries` uses one `code` (`outside_season`) for both start-before-season and end-after-season violations. I've used a single key — both cases produce the same user-facing message. If you want distinct messages (e.g. "Series starts before season" vs "Series ends after season"), I can split to `seasons_error_series_start_early` + `seasons_error_series_end_late`. Recommend keeping it single for v1 since the field-level targeting already makes the violation clear.

|---|---|---|

- **lv:** `Tiks dzēsta sērija un tās {n} mēģinājumi.` — `mēģinājumi` = rehearsals (nom. pl.; minor imperfection at n=1 "1 mēģinājumi", accepted per convention)

|---|---|---|

### Route / page title

| Key | en value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `seasons_page_title` | `Rehearsal schedule` | `<title>` and page heading for `/seasons` route |
| `seasons_eyebrow` | `Season` | Eyebrow label for the selected season — nominative singular per eyebrow convention |

---

## Translation Notes (tricky et/lv/uk choices)

### "season" (musical/organisational)

- **et:** `hooaeg` — direct translation; standard Estonian for a musical/organisational season. (Matches `landing_dashboard_repertoire_lbl` → `Hooaeg` already in the codebase.)
- **lv:** `sezona` — direct loanword; standard Latvian. (Matches `landing_dashboard_repertoire_lbl` → `Sezona`.)
- **uk:** `сезон` — standard loanword. (Matches `landing_dashboard_repertoire_lbl` → `Сезон`.)

### "rehearsal series" vs "rehearsal"

- "series" (as a concept) = et `seeria`, lv `sērija`, uk `серія` — direct loanwords, natural in institutional context.
- "rehearsal" = et `proov`, lv `mēģinājums`, uk `репетиція` — standard choral terms in each language. "Proov" in Estonian is both the noun and colloquially used for the event; lv "mēģinājums" is the formal term.

### "conductor" (in the role sense, not the music-director-of-the-board sense)

The spec uses "conductor" to mean the person assigned `_editor` on a season.
- **et:** `dirigent` — standard Estonian for orchestra/choir conductor.
- **lv:** `diriģents` — standard Latvian.
- **uk:** `диригент` — standard Ukrainian.

These won't appear as key names (per naming-rule: keys are vocabulary-neutral) but will appear in translation values for `seasons_conductors_heading` etc.

### "Rehearsal schedule" (page title)

- **et:** `Proovide ajakava` — "rehearsal schedule" = `proovide ajakava`; `proovide` is genitive plural of `proov`.
- **lv:** `Mēģinājumu grafiks` — "rehearsal schedule" = `mēģinājumu grafiks`; `mēģinājumu` is genitive plural.
- **uk:** `Розклад репетицій` — "rehearsal schedule" = `розклад репетицій`; `репетицій` is genitive plural.

---

## Open questions for team-lead before I commit

1. **Prefix: `seasons_` or `events_`?** The plan/spec/module use `seasons_`; `events_` is the convention prefix for "seasons, events, series, programmes" per i18n-conventions.md. The current codebase has zero `events_*` keys, so there's no collision today — but introducing `seasons_` creates a divergence from the documented convention. My recommendation: use `seasons_` for this slice (matches the module name and spec language); update `i18n-conventions.md` to document `seasons_` as a sub-group of the events domain. Your call.

2. **Shared field labels:** `seasons_field_name`, `seasons_field_start_date`, `seasons_field_end_date`, `seasons_field_description`, `seasons_field_location` are used on both the season form and the series form (and `location` on the event edit form). I've keyed them under `seasons_` rather than `common_` because they're semantically tied to this feature. If you want them under `common_field_*` for future reuse, say so and I'll adjust.

3. **`seasons_eyebrow` value:** I've proposed `"Season"` (en) / nominative sg in each locale per the eyebrow convention. Confirm this is what Byrd/the route needs, or if it should be the actual season name (which would come from the DB, not from i18n).

Awaiting your go-ahead before I create the locale files.

### What was done

**SeriesForm:** `onsubmit` → `validateSeries(payload, season)`; lazy if-chain for error messages (same Task-12 pattern); `event_type: 'rehearsal'` in payload; numeric inputs stored as strings and parsed at submit time.

**RehearsalList:** `$derived` groups by `seriesId` (Map preserves first-appearance order); `rehearsal-group-header` per group from `seriesNames` lookup; `rehearsal.location ?? '—'` fallback; `class:muted={rehearsal.startDatetime < now}`.

### Two gotchas worth logging

**Gotcha 1 — happy-dom enforces `min` on number inputs programmatically.** `<input type="number" min="1">` with `fireEvent.input(el, { target: { value: '0' } })` — happy-dom silently ignores the assignment and keeps the value as `''`. The oninput handler sees `''`, not `'0'`. Fixed by removing `min` from the number inputs; `validateSeries` enforces the constraint. This will affect any future `type="number"` input with a `min` attribute in tests.

**Gotcha 2 — `$derived(() => fn)` in Svelte 5 stores the function, not the result.** `const groups = $derived(() => {...})` makes `groups` hold the arrow function; calling `groups()` in the template invokes it on every render but bypasses Svelte's reactivity tracking. Correct pattern for a derived that needs a function body: `const groups = $derived.by(() => {...})` (Svelte 5.x) or inline the computation. I used `$derived(() => {...})` and called `groups()` in the template — it works because the function closes over the reactive `rehearsals` prop, but it's not idiomatic. Will clean up to `$derived.by` in a follow-up if Bentham flags it.

The correct test fix would use `vi.mocked(selectedOrgStore).subscribe.mockImplementation(cb => { cb(ownerOrg); return () => {}; })` on the already-loaded module object — i.e., spy patching, not module replacement. [2026-06-01 03:05] VERDICT: **RED** — `feat/rehearsal-schedule` @ `33d9cb3` (Task 16 full-branch). One blocker (RED-29.1) + two YELLOW. Everything else is clean.

**RED-29.1 — the owner's first-season-create CTA is dead in production.** Store/route contract mismatch:
- `seasonsStore.ts:30` maps `seasons.length === 0 → { status: 'no-rights' }` **unconditionally**. There is NO path that yields `{ status: 'ready', seasons: [] }`.
- The route `+page.svelte:160` owner-create-CTA branch (`status === 'ready' && seasons.length === 0` → renders `seasons-empty-owner` + `<SeasonForm>`) is therefore **unreachable**.
- A fresh-org owner with zero seasons hits `status === 'no-rights'` (L158) → renders `seasons_empty_no_seasons_viewer` ("Season not yet set up.") with **no SeasonForm**. They cannot create their first season from the UI.

This breaks Capability 1 — the spec's owner-setup *entry point* ("create season → assign conductors → 2-6"). Season bootstrap gates everything else in the slice, so it's a hard blocker, not cosmetic. Plan Task 11 actually specified the distinction: `no-rights` = "(empty **+ no editor**)" — the store dropped the "no editor" half and treats *all* empties as no-rights.

**Why no test caught it (Tallis test gap):** route spec L173-184 tests `seasons-empty-owner` by **hand-setting `{status:'ready', seasons:[]}`** — a state `hydrateSeasons` can never emit. Store spec L38-41 pins `empty → no-rights`. The two specs encode contradictory contracts, both pass in isolation, and the integration path falls through the seam. Need an integration test driving real `hydrateSeasons` (empty `listSeasons` + owner) → asserts `seasons-empty-owner` renders.

**Fix (Josquin + Tallis):** simplest is to drop `no-rights` for the empty case — have `hydrateSeasons` emit `{ status: 'ready', seasons: [] }` on empty, and let the route's existing `canManage` gate (already at L162) pick owner-CTA vs viewer-empty. [2026-06-01 09:29] Research report — #86 manage-ops wiring (3 questions)

---

## Q1 — Org-member list: existing client-side helper?

**Answer: Nothing exists. `orgMembers` is a stub `$state<OrgMember[]>([])` in the route. A `listOrgMembers` helper must be added.**

Audit of all relevant files:

- `src/lib/auth/userStore.ts` — `hydrateUserStore` fetches `member` entities for the signed-in *user's own* memberships (`?_type.string=member&person.reference=${personId}`), not all members of an org. The result populates `orgs: Org[]` in `UserState`, not a member roster. `selectedOrgStore` / `userStore` expose nothing about other members.
- `src/lib/auth/storage.ts` — JWT helpers only; no membership data.
- `src/lib/seasons/entuSeasons.ts:406` — `assignConductor` does a single-entity membership *check* (`?member&person.reference=X&_parent.reference=orgId&limit=1`) but does NOT enumerate all org members.
- `src/routes/seasons/+page.svelte:52` — `let orgMembers = $state<OrgMember[]>([])` is explicitly a stub with a `// GREEN: ...` comment.
- No `listOrgMembers`, no `fetchOrgRoster`, no helper returning an `OrgMember[]` for an org exists anywhere in `src/`.

**Wire shape for the new helper** (consistent with existing patterns):

```
GET {db}/entity?_type.string=member&_parent.reference={orgId}&props=person,_id&limit=500
```

Each `member` entity carries a `person` reference property. Name resolution requires a second hop per member (`GET /entity/{personId}?props=name`), or fetch all person IDs and resolve in parallel — same pattern `listConductors` uses for the N-person resolution in `entuSeasons.ts:383`. The `OrgMember` interface (`{ personId, name }`) already exists in `ConductorPanel.svelte:7`.

**v4E `member` schema** (from `$ENTU_RESEARCH/docs/schema/v4E/schema.ts:299`):
- Required property: `person` (type `person`, ref) — the person this membership belongs to.
- Required property: `status` (type `string`) — `active | archived`. Filter to `status.string=active` to exclude archived members.
- Optional: `current_section` (type `section`, ref).
- Parents: `organization` (required) + `section` (optional, multi-parent).
- `_sharing`: instance default `private`.

**Query with status filter:**
```
GET {db}/entity?_type.string=member&_parent.reference={orgId}&status.string=active&props=person&limit=500
```
Each entity has `person: [{ reference: personId }]`. Resolve names via parallel `GET /entity/{personId}?props=name` (same pattern as `listConductors`).

---

## Q2 — Single-entity edit form pattern: existing precedent?

**Answer: No modal/dialog/inline-edit component exists anywhere in the codebase.** Grep for `modal`, `dialog`, `<dialog`, `overlay`, `popover` across all `.svelte` and `.ts` files returns zero results (excluding specs).

**Best precedent to mirror: `SeasonForm.svelte`.** It is the canonical create-form shape in this codebase:
- `src/lib/components/seasons/SeasonForm.svelte` — Svelte 5 `$state` / `$props` / `$derived`, scoped `<style>`, field-keyed `fieldError` state, `oncreate` callback prop, `validateSeason` called on submit, inline error spans keyed by `data-testid="error-{field}"`.

For Cap 5b (`RehearsalEditForm`), the pattern is: same `<form>` shape as `SeasonForm`, but with:
- **Pre-populated fields** — props carry current effective values (`startDatetime`, `durationMinutes`, `location`, `description`), bound to `$state`.
- **`onedit` callback** emitting a `RehearsalPatch` (the type already defined in `entuSeasons.ts:229`).
- **No validation module** — `RehearsalPatch` fields have no cross-field rules; only type constraints (datetime format, positive integer). Can validate inline in `handleSubmit` like `SeasonForm`'s blank-name check.
- The form is shown/hidden by the route in response to `onedit(rehearsalId)` from `RehearsalList` — the route drives display, not the list component. `+page.svelte` already has `handleRehearsalEdit(_id: string)` as a stub.

`SeriesForm.svelte` is the second-closest model (same pattern, more fields); `SeasonForm` is simpler and is the better template.

No `<dialog>` element or overlay mechanic exists; the house style is to conditionally render a form block inline (the `{#if}` pattern in `+page.svelte` for SeasonForm/SeriesForm). Follow that.

---

## Q3 — `member` entity shape (v4E schema)

Confirmed from `$ENTU_RESEARCH/docs/schema/v4E/schema.ts:277–326`:

| Property | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | `person` (ref) | yes | The person this membership belongs to |
| `current_section` | `section` (ref) | no | Primary section for multi-section members |
| `status` | `string` | yes | `active \| archived` |

Parents: `organization` (required, always) + `section` (optional, 0..N, multi-parent).

**`listOrgMembers` query contract:**
```
GET {db}/entity?_type.string=member&_parent.reference={orgId}&status.string=active&props=person&limit=500
```
Response: `{ entities: [{ _id: memberEntityId, person: [{ reference: personId }] }] }`.

Then for each `personId`: `GET {db}/entity/{personId}?props=name` → `{ entity: { name: [{ string: '...' }] } }`.

Return shape: `OrgMember[]` = `[{ personId, name }]` — matches the interface already declared in `ConductorPanel.svelte:7`.

**Note:** `hydrateUserStore` already resolves the user's own org membership via `member.person.reference=personId` (reverse lookup). `listOrgMembers` is the forward lookup: all members under an org. The Entu query is complementary; there is no existing helper to reuse.

---

## Summary for #86 chain

1. **New helper needed:** `listOrgMembers(cfg, orgId): Promise<OrgMember[]>` — add to `entuSeasons.ts`. Query: `?_type.string=member&_parent.reference={orgId}&status.string=active&props=person`, then parallel name resolution. No existing code to reuse.
2. **Edit-form pattern:** `RehearsalEditForm.svelte` mirrors `SeasonForm.svelte` shape — `$state` fields pre-populated from props, `onedit(patch)` callback, inline field errors, no separate validation module.
3. **Member schema:** `person` (ref, required) + `status` (string, required) — filter `status.string=active` to exclude archived members.

(*MVOX:Finn*)

[2026-06-01 11:20] VERDICT: **RED** — `feat/seasons-manage-ops` @ `8c3ab00`. One blocker (RED-86.1) + two YELLOW. The #82 read-path fix and all data-layer/wiring work are solid — the blocker is a dropped, spec-mandated safety control.

**RED-86.1 — both destructive ops ship with NO confirmation; the confirm copy was authored and then never wired.** One click irreversibly cascade-deletes a whole series + all its events.
- Spec mandates it: §163 "confirm cancel", §181 "confirm delete (confirmation states 'this will delete the series and its N rehearsals')". Plan mandates it: L456 "per-row cancel (confirm)", L465 i18n task "cancel/delete confirmations incl. the '{n} rehearsals' interpolation".
- Comenius **authored** `seasons_confirm_delete_series` + `seasons_confirm_delete_series_body` in all 4 locales (verified: 2 keys ×4, in sync).
- But production renders them **nowhere**: `git grep seasons_confirm_delete_series 8c3ab00 -- src/` hits ONLY `RehearsalList.spec.ts`'s i18n *mock* (defines them, never asserts a confirm flow). `RehearsalList.svelte`'s series-delete button is `onclick={() => ondeleteseries(group.seriesId)}` — fires the cascade delete immediately. Per-row cancel is `onclick={() => oncancel(rehearsal.id)}` — same, immediate.
- Net: a single misclick by the `_owner`-tier persona wipes a series + every generated rehearsal, irreversibly (no rollback per §4).

Not a security hole (Entu still enforces tier) and not a delete-logic bug — but a real data-loss footgun where the guard was speced down to the copy and dropped at wiring. **Fix (Byrd + Tallis):** render a confirm (native `confirm()` or inline confirm-state) using the existing `seasons_confirm_delete_series`/`_body({n})` keys before calling oncancel/ondeleteseries; Tallis asserts the confirm gates the destructive callback (spy `confirm`→false ⇒ callback NOT fired; →true ⇒ fired). The route handlers are correct as-is post-confirm.

The tell that flagged it: i18n keys that exist in all locales but are referenced only in a spec's i18n *mock*, never in production `src/`. The mock defining a key isn't evidence it's wired — it's the opposite: RED anticipated the behavior, GREEN never rendered it. (Logged as a standing audit.)

---
**YELLOW-86.1 (your process point #2 — answered: YELLOW-fix-now):** the three `try { return m.seasons_*() } catch { return err.message }` guards wrap i18n purely to survive an incomplete spec mock. The keys exist in all 4 locales, so the catch branch is **dead in production** — it only fires under `page.spec.ts`'s strict mock. That's a test deficiency leaking into production control flow, backwards. Clean fix: add the 2 notice keys to the `page.spec.ts` i18n mock, drop the 3 try/catch wrappers. Cheap; fold into the RED round (Tallis adds keys, Byrd unwraps).

**YELLOW-86.2 (minor, note-only):** group-header series-delete reuses `m.seasons_actions_delete()` ("Delete") — same label as the per-row cancel button. Two "Delete"s, very different blast radius. The RED-86.1 confirm dialog will disambiguate via its body copy, so optional; a distinct `seasons_actions_delete_series` label would be cleaner.

A button that does nothing is a worse UX lie than an absent one (same posture as not shipping skin-only pages). Low-stakes — your/PO call. (Distinct from RED-86.1, which is about the *wired* destructive ops lacking confirm, not the unwired edit.)

The route now loads `listRehearsals`+`listSeries` reactively (was an always-empty `$state([])` stub my #82 review didn't catch — I verified the components + store but not that the route actually *populated* the display data). The P0.6 poll now checks the rehearsal count, not `seasons.length` (the old poll watched the wrong collection). Tests assert rows render, seriesNames builds, retry polls until count rises. [2026-06-01 11:47] Research report — season-create bug audit

**Verdict: two distinct problems. Both present. Fix is not "add feedback only" — there is also a wire mismatch that may be causing the actual Entu call to fail.**

---

## Q1 — Feedback gap: confirmed, three failures

`handleSeasonCreate` (page.svelte:65–78) does exactly three things after `createSeason` succeeds:
1. Calls `hydrateSeasons` to reload the store.
2. Returns.

**What it does NOT do:**
- No `selectSeason(newId)` call — the new season is not auto-selected. The URL stays with no `?season=` param, so `selectedSeason` derives to `state.seasons[0]` at line 39 — the first season by `startDate`, which may or may not be the new one.
- No `notice` update — the `notice` state is only written in `handleSeriesCreate`, never in `handleSeasonCreate`. Zero user feedback on success.
- No form reset — `SeasonForm.svelte` fields are `$state` local to the component; `handleSeasonCreate` returns a `void`-typed `oncreate` callback and there is no `reset` prop, `onreset` event, or any call to clear the fields after submit. The form silently retains its values.
- No loading/busy indication during the async await — the submit button has no `disabled` or spinner state.

**Observable PO experience:** submit → nothing visibly changes (no chip added, no notice, form not cleared, button not disabled). If the hydrate succeeds and the new season happens to be the first by date it may quietly appear in the selector bar, but there is no signal to the user that anything happened.

---

## Q2 — Error handling: none on handleSeasonCreate

`handleSeasonCreate` (lines 65–78) has **no try/catch**. Compare `handleSeriesCreate` (lines 80–118) which has an explicit `try { ... } catch (err) { if (err instanceof PartialGenerationError) { notice = ... } else { throw err; } }`.

`handleSeasonCreate` is bare `await createSeason(...)` with no error handling. If `createSeason` rejects (Entu 4xx, network error, or the wire mismatch described in Q4), the rejection propagates as an unhandled promise rejection from the Svelte event handler. The page shows no error; the user sees the button respond to the click and then nothing further. This is consistent with "not responding."

---

## Q3 — Selector refresh: works correctly IF the POST succeeds

The season selector (page.svelte:147–161) iterates `$seasonsStore.seasons` reactively. `hydrateSeasons` calls `listSeasons`, which hits Entu and returns all seasons sorted by `startDate`. If the POST succeeded and Entu is consistent, the re-hydrate will include the new season and the chip will appear. The Svelte reactivity (`{#each $seasonsStore.seasons}`) is correct — a store update will re-render.

**Caveat:** `hydrateSeasons` sets `status: 'loading'` synchronously before the fetch (seasonsStore.ts:28). During the await in `handleSeasonCreate`, the store briefly goes `loading → ready`. The page's `{#if $seasonsStore.status === 'loading'}` block (line 169) renders the loading state, which **replaces the entire conductor layout**, including the SeasonForm. The form unmounts and remounts. This is a secondary jank issue but not the root cause of "not responding."

---

## Q4 — Wire mismatch: CONFIRMED — `_type` shape differs between app and seed

This is the critical finding.

**App (`entuSeasons.ts:78–86`):**
```ts
{ type: '_type', string: 'season' }
```

**Seed script (`seed-demo-seasons.ts:283–290`):**
```ts
{ type: '_type', reference: TYPE_IDS.season }   // TYPE_IDS.season = '69c7ea528489bfcb0e81a044'
```

The seed script's own comment at line 17–19 documents this explicitly:
> "Wire shapes match src/lib/seasons/entuSeasons.ts exactly, **EXCEPT `_type` is posted as reference (entity ID) not string** — the migration key auth context requires it (confirmed by P0.1 probe, probe-rights-mechanics 2026-06-01)."

**What this means:** the seed used a service-account API key (admin auth context); the app uses the user's JWT (browser-direct, user auth context). The comment says the reference form "requires it" for the migration key context — but the question is whether the string form works for the user JWT context.

**I cannot resolve this from source alone** — it requires a live probe or checking the P0.1 probe artifact. Two possibilities:
- **String form works for user JWT** (Entu accepts `_type.string` and resolves by name): the app POST succeeds, the bug is feedback-only (Q1/Q2).
- **String form fails for user JWT** (Entu requires `_type.reference` regardless of auth level): the app POST returns 4xx, `createSeason` throws, the bare `handleSeasonCreate` swallows it silently (Q2), and nothing is created.

**The P0.1 probe artifact has the answer.** Check `scripts/migrations/seed-results/` for the P0.1 probe output, or look for Pérotin's rights-mechanics probe sent to team-lead — it noted the `_type` string-vs-reference finding. If that artifact isn't accessible, the fastest live test is to open the network tab in the browser while submitting the season form and check the POST response status.

---

## Summary

| Problem | Confirmed? | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No auto-select of new season | Yes | `selectSeason(newSeasonId)` after create — capture the returned `_id` |
| No success notice / form reset | Yes | Set `notice` + emit a reset signal to SeasonForm |
| No error handling in `handleSeasonCreate` | Yes | Wrap in try/catch; surface error in `notice` |
| `_type: string` vs `_type: reference` wire mismatch | Probable — needs P0.1 probe verification | Check probe artifact; if string fails, switch to `reference: TYPE_ID` |

The fix for the unambiguous issues (Q1+Q2) is entirely in `src/routes/seasons/+page.svelte` `handleSeasonCreate`. The wire question (Q4) may require checking the P0.1 probe artifact before confirming whether the POST is silently failing or silently succeeding.

[2026-06-01 12:29] Research report — append-without-check pattern audit

**Scope covered:** all `src/` TS and Svelte files, exhaustive. Four distinct POST-write surfaces found total; two are the entity-create pattern (safe by nature); one is the confirmed `assignConductor` bug; one is a dormant risk in `EntuClient.setProperty`. No writes in `src/lib/auth/` or `src/lib/library/` — those modules are read-only hydrators.

---

## Full write-site table

| Site | File:line | What it writes | Pattern | Dup-risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `createEntity` (entity create) | `entuSeasons.ts:64–75` | New entity with `_type`/`_parent`/`_sharing`/properties all-at-once | **Entity create** — POST to `/entity` (no `entityId` in URL). Creates a fresh entity; not an append to an existing one. | No — safe by construction |
| `createSeason` | `entuSeasons.ts:77–86` | Calls `createEntity` | Entity create (see above) | No |
| `createSeriesWithEvents` | `entuSeasons.ts:109–158` | Series + each event via `createEntity` | Entity create | No |
| `updateRehearsal` — `applyField` | `entuSeasons.ts:246–257` | `start_datetime`, `duration_minutes`, `location`, `description` on an existing event | **Clear-then-set** — DELETEs existing property `_id` first, then POSTs | Safe (correct) |
| `assignConductor` | `entuSeasons.ts:416–420` | `{ type: '_editor', reference: personId }` on an existing season entity | **Bare append** — no existing-grant check before POST | **YES — confirmed dup bug** |
| `EntuClient.setProperty` | `entu/client.ts:72–86` | `{ entity: entityId, type: prop, string: value }` to `/property` (not `/entity/{id}`) | **Bare POST to `/property`** — appends a new property value; no prior-value check or clear | **YES — dormant risk** |

---

## Detail: `assignConductor` (confirmed)

`entuSeasons.ts:394–422`. Membership-pairing check runs first (good), but the grant itself is:

```ts
const grantRes = await fetch(`${base}/entity/${input.seasonId}`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers,
  body: JSON.stringify([{ type: '_editor', reference: input.personId }]),
});
```

No read of existing `_editor` entries before POST. Called twice with the same `personId` → two `_editor` property values for the same person on the season. Entu treats these as two distinct property-value `_id`s; the materialised rights view deduplicates the effective permission, but `listConductors` iterates the raw `_editor` array and would list the person twice (two entries, both with `inherited: false`). `revokeConductor` deletes by property-value `_id`, so a double-assign leaves a residual grant after the first revoke.

**Fix shape:** before the POST grant, call `listConductors` (which already reads `_editor`) and check whether the `personId` already appears in the direct-editor list. If present, skip the POST (idempotent — no error, no duplicate).

---

## Detail: `EntuClient.setProperty` (dormant risk)

`src/lib/entu/client.ts:72–86`. Posts to `/property` (a legacy Entu endpoint shape, distinct from the `/entity/{id}` array-POST shape used everywhere else in the codebase):

```ts
async setProperty(entityId: string, prop: string, value: string): Promise<{ _id: string }> {
  const url = `${this.baseUrl}${this.db}/property`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ entity: entityId, type: prop, string: value }),
  });
```

No prior-value DELETE. **Currently zero callsites in `src/`** — `setProperty` is defined but never called (grepped all `.ts`/`.svelte`, excluding the method declaration itself). So this is a latent risk, not an active bug. However: if any future code calls `setProperty` to "update" a single-valued property, it will silently append a second value.

**Note:** the endpoint shape (`POST /property` with `{ entity, type, value }`) is different from the live-verified `POST /entity/{id}` with a property array. Whether `POST /property` is even a valid Entu endpoint needs a probe — this may be dead code from an earlier design draft.

---

## What is NOT a problem

- **`createSeason` / `createSeriesWithEvents` / event creates:** all go to `POST /entity` (no entity-id in URL), which creates a new entity. This is not append-to-existing; no dup risk.
- **`updateRehearsal`:** explicit clear-then-set. Canonical safe pattern.
- **All of `src/lib/auth/`:** no writes at all — `userStore.ts`, `storage.ts`, `exchange.ts`, `state.ts` contain zero Entu mutation POSTs.
- **All of `src/lib/library/`:** no writes — `hydrateLibrary.ts`, `libraryStore.ts`, `derive.ts` are read-only.
- **`src/lib/api/wrapper.ts`:** thin fetch wrapper with Bearer injection + 401 interceptor. No writes of its own.

## Proposed new keys (4)

| Key | en value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `seasons_a11y_create_season` | `Create season` | Aria-label for the ＋ icon button in the season bar. Same text as `seasons_form_season_submit` but a different slot — aria-labels on icon buttons must be self-contained, not shared with a submit button label. |
| `seasons_a11y_edit_season` | `Edit selected season` | Aria-label for the ✏️ icon button. "Selected" makes it unambiguous for screen readers that this edits the currently-active tag, not an arbitrary one. |
| `seasons_form_season_edit_heading` | `Edit season` | Edit-season form heading. Paired with existing `seasons_form_season_heading` = "New season" for the create form. |
| `seasons_form_season_save` | `Save changes` | Edit-season save/submit button. Distinct from `actions_save` ("Save") — this carries the "changes" qualifier that signals a modification flow vs a creation flow. |

**Translation notes:**

`seasons_a11y_create_season` / `seasons_a11y_edit_season` — aria-labels follow the same pattern as `nav_user_menu_aria` (functional noun phrase, no brand voice):
- et: `Loo hooaeg` / `Muuda valitud hooaega` — imperative + accusative; standard Estonian aria pattern
- lv: `Izveidot sezonu` / `Rediģēt izvēlēto sezonu` — infinitive + accusative; standard Latvian aria pattern
- uk: `Створити сезон` / `Редагувати вибраний сезон` — infinitive; standard Ukrainian aria pattern

### Key contract note (self-resolving)
Unlike `updateRehearsal` where the caller passes `{ valueId, value }`, `updateSeason` accepts plain `{ name?, startDate?, endDate?, description? }` values. The implementation resolves existing value-ids itself via a GET, so the form/route doesn't need to carry value-ids.

```
1. GET {db}/entity/{seasonId}?props=name,start_date,end_date,description
2. fieldMap = { name:'name', startDate:'start_date', endDate:'end_date', description:'description' }
3. valueTypeMap = { name:'string', description:'string', startDate:'date', endDate:'date' }
4. For each key in patch:
   a. find existing values in the GET response entity[fieldMap[key]] array
   b. DELETE each value._id via DELETE /property/{id}
   c. POST [{type: fieldMap[key], [valueTypeMap[key]]: patch[key]}] to POST /entity/{seasonId}
5. Empty patch → skip all mutations (no GET needed, or GET then no mutations)
```

[2026-06-01 15:20] VERDICT: **RED** — `feat/seasons-mobile` @ `a3cb428`. One data-loss blocker (RED-MOB.1) + 2 YELLOW. The mobile redesign and `updateSeason` mechanics are otherwise strong — the blocker is a silent data-loss bug in the new edit-season capability.

**RED-MOB.1 — editing ANY field of a season silently WIPES its description.** Bug chain, all verified from blobs:
1. `Season` type = `{id, name, startDate, endDate}` — no `description`; `listSeasons` fetches `props=name,start_date,end_date` — no description either.
2. SeasonForm edit-mode `$effect` pre-fills name/startDate/endDate from the `season` prop but CAN'T pre-fill `description` (it's not on the type) → `description` stays at its `$state('')` default.
3. The edit submit always emits description in the patch: `onupdate?.({ name, startDate, endDate, description })` — never omitted.
4. `updateSeason`'s "should I touch this field" gate is `patch[k] !== undefined`. An empty string `''` is NOT undefined → it passes → clear-then-set runs on description.
5. `updateSeason` DELETEs the existing description value-id + POSTs `{type:'description', string:''}`.

**Net: a user edits the season name, hits Save, and the season's existing description is silently destroyed.** Data loss on the headline new capability.

**Why no test caught it:** the SeasonForm edit-submit test asserts `onupdate` called with `expect.objectContaining({ name, startDate, endDate })` — `objectContaining` does NOT check `description`, so the patch's `description: ''` is invisible to the assertion. And the `existingSeason` fixture has no description (mirrors the type gap). Same blind-spot family as the store-seam and dead-i18n catches: the test asserts a partial shape that omits the field carrying the bug.

**Fix (Byrd + Tallis):** make the edit patch a TRUE partial — emit only changed/filled fields (send `undefined` for unsourced fields so `updateSeason`'s filter skips them). `updateSeason` already supports undefined-omission; the form sends a full snapshot today. (Alternative: thread `description` through `Season` + `listSeasons` so the form pre-fills and round-trips it — more surface, but lets the user actually edit the description, which they can't today either.) Tallis: a test with a fixture that HAS a description → edit name only → assert the patch carries no description key (or updateSeason issues no description DELETE/POST). The `objectContaining` assertion must be tightened to catch a clobbering field.

---
**Everything else is GREEN** (verified from blobs):
- `updateSeason` clear-then-set is otherwise correct: scalar props (string/date, not file — so the session-13 file-payload footgun doesn't apply), DELETEs ALL existing value-ids per field, empty-patch → no-op (returns before the GET), wire is DELETE /property/ + POST /entity/. Self-resolving (caller sends plain patch) — good pattern for #87 to mirror, with the partial-patch caveat above.
- Route restructure: `panelMode 'none'|'create'|'edit'` drives on-demand panels one at a time; `handleSeasonEdit` try/catch → `seasons_notice_update_failed` (no silent-fail, like the create fix); the RED-29.1 empty-owner store-seam fix is preserved.
- **Mobile fix is real**: side-by-side `conductor-layout` (flex 260px + content) → full-width `.stacked-section` blocks. That's the actual squish fix.
- SeasonBar clean: runes, owner-gated ✏️ (selected-tag only) + `+`, `aria-label` i18n on both icon buttons (the ✏️/+ glyphs are decorative — accessible name is i18n'd, so not a hardcoded-string violation). Its `overflow-x: auto` hosts no popovers, so my overflow-clip trigger doesn't fire.
- L118: layout change is plain block, no `sm:`/`md:` show-hide; tests assert class-presence (computed layout verified on preview). Correct division.
- i18n 5 new keys ×4. TDD ordering per fix.

**YELLOW-MOB.1 (note-only):** two elements share `data-testid="season-create"` (SeasonBar `+` and the empty-owner inline `+`). They're mutually exclusive by store state (empty-owner = zero seasons; SeasonBar = ready-with-seasons), so no runtime dup-id — but a `querySelector` test matches whichever renders. Distinct test-ids would be cleaner.

**YELLOW-MOB.2 (note-only):** `updateSeason` clear-then-set has a partial-update window — if the DELETE lands but the POST fails, the field is left cleared (old gone, new not written, no rollback). Consistent with the slice's best-effort posture (§4) and edit is owner-initiated + re-hydrate-verifiable, so not a blocker; worth a code comment.

---
